Hertsmere's population increased by around 7,800 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 110,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Hertsmere increased by 7.8%, from around 100,000 in 2011 to around 107,800 in 2021.

The population here increased at a similar rate to the overall population of the East of England (8.3%), but by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Hertsmere was home to around 7.6 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 7.1 in 2011. This area was among the top 45% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Hertsmere than across the East of England

Median age in Hertsmere

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Hertsmere increased by one year, from 39 to 40 years of age.

This area had a slightly lower average (median) age than the East of England as a whole in 2021 (41 years) but had a similar averaage (median) age to England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 2,900 (an increase of 15.8%), while the number of residents between 20 and 24 years fell by just under 450 (7.2% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.4 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Hertsmere residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 81,300 Hertsmere residents said they were born in England. This represented 75.4% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 80,800 in 2011, which at the time represented 80.8% of Hertsmere's population.

Romania was the next most represented, with just over 3,300 Hertsmere residents reporting this country of birth (3.1%). This figure was up from around 600 in 2011, which at the time represented 0.6% of the population of Hertsmere.

The number of Hertsmere residents born in India rose from around 1,100 in 2011 (1.1% of the local population) to around 2,000 in 2021 (1.8%).

In 2021, 75.4% of Hertsmere residents reported their country of birth as England

Marriage and civil partnership in Hertsmere

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were married (or in a civil partnership) was greater across the East of England (2.9 percentage points) than in Hertsmere (0.5 percentage points).

In Hertsmere, the percentage of adults who were married or in a civil partnership decreased from 50.3% in 2011 to 49.8% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage decreased from 50.1% to 47.2%.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Hertsmere increased from 31.8% to 33.8%, while the percentage of adults who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 8.4% to 8.5%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who were married or in a civil partnership in Hertsmere decreased by 0.5 percentage points

Religion in Hertsmere

In 2021, 24.2% of Hertsmere residents reported having "No religion", up from 19.2% in 2011. The rise of 5.0 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Hertsmere. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the East of England, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.9% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 41.8% of people in Hertsmere described themselves as Christian (down from 51.7%), while 17.0% described themselves as Jewish (up from 14.3% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 24.2% of usual residents in Hertsmere reported having "No religion"

Rise in private renting

Of Hertsmere households, 17.3% rented privately in 2021, up from 12.5% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in Hertsmere (4.7 percentage points) than across the East of England (3.5 percentage points, from 14.7% to 18.2%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Private renting in Hertsmere increased by 4.7 percentage points

Unpaid care in Hertsmere

In 2021, 4.8% of Hertsmere residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.5% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Hertsmere (2.7 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the East of England (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Hertsmere decreased by 2.7 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Hertsmere

In 2021, 10.5% of Hertsmere residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 7.4% in 2011. The 3.1 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the East of England, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 4.8% to 6.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 77.1% of people in Hertsmere identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 85.0% in 2011), while 4.8% identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category (compared with 3.9% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 1.0% in 2011 to 3.8% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

Read the bulletin Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 10.5% of usual residents in Hertsmere identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

National identity in Hertsmere

In 2021, 11.6% of Hertsmere residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 9.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 40 people (2.7%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 1.3% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Hertsmere that identified as "British only" increased from 20.9% to 59.3%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK in Hertsmere (2.0 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the East of England (2.1 percentage points, from 6.9% to 9.0%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Hertsmere increased by 2.0 percentage points

Fewer couples without children

In 2021, 13.6% of Hertsmere households included a couple but no children. This figure decreased from 14.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in four households (23.0%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 23.2% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children increased from 7.3% to 7.9%.

This area had the region’s third lowest percentage of households including a couple but no children. Across the region, only Luton (11.7%) and Broxbourne (13.1%) had a lower percentage of households including a couple but no children.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Hertsmere decreased by 1.3 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Hertsmere residents aged 16 years and over, 59.8% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 60.5% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 40 people (2.8%) said they were unemployed, compared with 3.3% in 2011. The percentage of retired Hertsmere residents remained at 19.3%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater across the East of England (1.1 percentage points, from 58.4% to 57.3%) than in Hertsmere (0.7 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Hertsmere decreased by 0.7 percentage points

More adults worked short hours

Hertsmere saw the East of England's second-largest percentage-point rise in the proportion of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week (from 10.6% in 2011 to 12.3% in 2021).

Across the region, only North Norfolk saw a greater rise in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week (from 12.1% to 14.4%).

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Hertsmere increased by 1.6 percentage points

Disability in Hertsmere

In 2021, 5.9% of Hertsmere residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 7.2% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just over 1 in 12 people (8.4%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 8.8% in 2011. The proportion of Hertsmere residents who were not disabled increased from 84.0% to 85.7%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Hertsmere (1.3 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the East of England (1.2 percentage points, from 7.8% to 6.6%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Hertsmere decreased by 1.3 percentage points

Health in Hertsmere

In 2021, 52.3% of Hertsmere residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 49.4% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 33.8% to 32.6%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Hertsmere residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.9% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.4% to 3.1%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Hertsmere increased by 2.9 percentage points
